changes: Fourth-batch source-reviewed publication. Cross-verified from official 0.5 patch notes, current creator guides, an independent build guide, a planner, a current gameplay video and community questions.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: This is the Blood Mage crit entry point. It league-starts, explains the 100% crit gate, and then points to verified 0.5 variants (Comet, Ball Lightning / Volcano, and others) so you pick by stage rather than copying one config blindly.
This is a verification-first guide. The 100% crit gate, life-cost management and variant selection are described from current creator guides; the 'crit is not damage' ordering is the actionable core.

sections.title: Pros and Cons
pros: Strong league starter that scales into multiple endgame variants.
Blood Mage life-cost fantasy with recovery tools.
Crit gate gives a clear, repeatable power spike.
One hub page for several spell variants.
cons: 100% crit is a gate, not a damage guarantee.
Life cost must be managed or you self-damage.
Copying crit without skill level still feels weak.

sections.title: Is This Build Right For You?
paragraphs: Pick Crit Blood Mage if you want a spell crit hub that leagues-starts and then branches. It is not a single fixed config; it is the entry point that routes you to the right variant.

steps.label: Levels 1-30 - Campaign spell
body: Level with a basic spell (e.g. a starter fire/cold skill). Focus on life and resistances; the crit gate is not the priority yet.

steps.label: Levels 31-55 - Crit base
body: Add a basic crit node and life-cost recovery (Grim Feast, remnants). Choose your first variant once crit chance is workable.

steps.label: Levels 56+ - Variant commit
body: Commit to a variant (Comet, Ball Lightning/Volcano, or other) and specialize the tree and supports for it.

steps.label: Waystones - Endgame
body: Close the crit gate, then raise crit damage and skill level. Benchmark on T15 before chasing the full crit variant.

sections.title: Crit Is a Gate, Not a Damage Number
paragraphs: 100% crit means your hits crit - it does not mean they hit hard. The ordering is: crit stability first, then spell skill level, then increased/gain-as damage, then crit damage, then cast speed, then luxury.

whyUse: Used by the Comet crit variant.

mappingBossingDiff: Clear and single-target split by variant.

sections.title: Variant Selector
sections.caption: Pick the branch by your current stage and goal. Ball Lightning / Volcano has its own dedicated page.

sections.title: Mapping Rotation
paragraphs: For normal packs: use the clear variant (Ball Lightning or the chosen clear skill), keep moving, and let life remnants recover the cost. Save the boss skill for rares and bosses.

sections.title: Rare Rotation
paragraphs: For rares: switch to the boss-burst skill, confirm crit is stable, then burst. Use a defensive skill if the rare is dangerous; do not over-extend into a deadly modifier.

sections.title: Boss Rotation
paragraphs: For bosses: verify the variant's combo in the current client before treating the written order as final. Manage life cost during the fight - recover between bursts so you do not self-drain.

sections.title: Blood Mage Ascendancy
paragraphs: Blood Mage ties power to life cost and lifecycle: the ascendancy rewards casting through life and recovering it, which is why life remnants and recovery are part of the build, not optional extras.

sections.title: Passive Tree Approach
paragraphs: Different variants need different trees. Read the tree against your chosen variant and current crit chance; do not paste one universal tree. Start with life, resistances and a few crit nodes, then specialize.

recommendations: A crit wand/sceptre; spell skill level matters as much as crit early. The off-hand can be a focus.
Life and resistances first; an ES or hybrid base pairs with the life-cost fantasy.
Life, attributes, crit multi and a bit of cast speed. Do not over-invest before the crit gate is met.
Spell skill level, crit, life. Luxury only after the core is solved.

priorities.label: Critical Chance
priorities.reason: Must hit the crit gate first

steps.label: Starter -> Functional
body: Cap resistances, secure life, reach a workable crit chance. Manage life cost from the start.

steps.label: Functional -> Endgame
body: Close the crit gate, add crit multi and skill level for your variant.

steps.label: Endgame -> Luxury
body: Chase perfect crit gear and gem levels only after T15 is comfortable.

sections.title: Budget Variants
paragraphs: Starter uses a rare crit wand and basic life/resist gear. Functional Endgame closes the crit gate and specializes a variant. Luxury is perfect crit gear and gem levels - do not treat the creator's top crit as your default target.

sections.title: Life Cost and Recovery
paragraphs: Blood Mage spends life to cast. Grim Feast, life remnants and leech keep the pool positive; if recovery lags, you self-drain during boss bursts. Treat recovery as a damage enabler, not a side note.

sections.title: Defensive Layers
paragraphs: Life plus a recoverable pool (energy shield or leech) is the baseline. Because you spend life to cast, defense and recovery are the same system - a thin pool both kills your damage and your survival.

sections.title: Community Voices

entries.label: Reddit - crit cap
entries.statement: Players ask whether 100% crit is required everywhere. The consensus: it is the boss gate; mapping can run lower until you can afford it.

entries.label: Forum - damage
entries.statement: Common report: 100% crit still feels weak because skill level and crit multi were skipped. The gate is necessary, not sufficient.

entries.label: Guide comments - life
entries.statement: Players note that ignoring remnants/leech leads to self-drain during boss bursts; recovery must be built in.

sections.note: Short paraphrases of common community questions and concerns, edited for clarity. Not verbatim quotes.

items.question: Is 100% crit the start or the end?
answer: It is the boss-variant gate. Early characters run a non-crit mapping combo and only close it before bossing.

items.question: Why does copying 100% crit still leave damage low?
answer: Crit is one multiplier. Skill level, increased damage and crit multi must follow; the gate alone is not enough.

items.question: Which variant should I pick?
answer: Campaign uses the verified league-start route; early maps use the crit base; Ball Lightning fans use Ballcano (separate page); high invest uses the full crit variant.

items.question: How do I keep from self-draining?
answer: Build in Grim Feast, life remnants and leech so the life pool stays positive during boss bursts; recovery lags are what cause self-drain.

checks: Add spell skill level and crit multi next; the crit gate is necessary but not sufficient on its own.
Add or fix life remnants / leech / Grim Feast so recovery keeps pace with life-cost casting.
